content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text resolves the Isaiah 7:14 link by treating the sign’s chapter bounds, Matthew 1:23’s application, and the almah/bethulah word-count as the deciding points, so it is addressing the kind of pressed-witness collision K-C governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse: the judge must assess the combined chain's footing rather than balance isolated verse points; I read the judge as balancing isolated verse points.", "why": "The judge treats the sign’s chapter bounds, Matthew 1:23’s application, and the almah/bethulah word-count as separate balancing points instead of weighing the pressed chain against the responding chain by footing."}
